newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest weather remains cool, mostly dry - WSC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest weather remains cool, mostly dry - WSC.

text.p: The U.S. Midwest should remain cool and mostly dry for the next couple of days, ahead of showers expected to move across the region this weekend, Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio.
"Mostly fair weather dominates right across the region today, the only exceptions being eastern Nebraska and north east Kansas," he said, noting those areas would receive scattered thunderstorms.
Burgio said there continued to be some concern about crops in the central Midwest where conditions have been drier than normal but cool temperatures were limiting crop stress.
"From the southeast corner of Iowa through central areas of Illinois they have had less than 50 percent of their normal rainfall since the June 1," Burgio said.

He noted the only showers in the Midwest on Wednesday had been in Ohio early in the day but temperatures had been cool with a high in Dayton, Ohio of 69 degrees Fahrenheit and in Mason City, Iowa of 68 degrees F. Most other areas of the U.S. Midwest had highs in the low 70s F to mid 80s F.

Temperatures on Thursday were seen warming only slightly with highs in the 70s F to mid 80s F. They should start to warm up Saturday when highs are likely to be in the 80s F to low 90s F, WSC's Burgio said.
Scattered showers and thunderstorms were forecast for the western Corn Belt on Saturday and the eastern Corn Belt on Sunday with coverage ranging from 40 to 70 percent, he said.
Rainfall totals should range from 0.25 to 1.00 inch, locally heavier. Burgio said it was not yet clear if dry areas in the central Midwest would receive much rain.
"We're not convinced that coverage will be that great. They may miss out in that area again," he said.
